events.summary:
H1 is adequately proven for the purpose of an active SEV-2 root cause. The causal chain now rests on verified findings at every hop except one explicitly-labelled mechanism link, and every competing hypothesis has been tested and contradicted by data rather than dismissed by argument.

Grounding: cfg-3120 (pricing-engine flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5->100, 12:04:00Z, pm-experiments) is verified with exact timestamp, and F31/F32 show it is the only change after 11:56Z and was never rolled back or reduced. The outcome side is verified at 60s resolution: CPU 38.22% (12:04) -> 98.65% (12:05) and p99 60.53ms -> 2534.9ms (12:05), same minute (F26/F27), with pricing-engine error_rate following one minute later 0.15% -> 12.98% (F29) and holding ~12.5% (F23); order-service's only error type is the 2500ms pricing-engine quote timeout, first at 12:06:10Z (F13/F43/F44), with p99 pinned just above the 2500ms budget (F45) and a single error step at the same 12:05Z bucket (F46). The fingerprint on the failing path is an internal compute deadline, 'GreeksV2Calculator: Monte-Carlo paths=20000 took 6465ms' and 'deadline exceeded computing quote calculator=GreeksV2', with zero connection-refused/parse/deserialization errors anywhere (F17/F43/F44). The one non-verified link (flag ramp -> the measured CPU is the Greeks v2 path) is honestly declared as an assumption; it is corroborated by exact-minute timing, flat offered load (F20/F21/F28), the compute-bound log signature, and the analogue precedent HIST-101 (F36). No per-flag metric exists in this dataset, so this cannot be closed by any query; that is a residual inferential hop, not a missing check.

Temporal order: onset is localized to the single minute bucket 12:05:00Z, one minute after the 12:04:00Z flag ramp and nine minutes after the 11:56:00Z market-data deploy; every minute 11:50-12:04Z is at baseline including the deploy minute (F26/F27/F30). The proposed cause immediately precedes onset.

Scope: the blast radius is fully explained by a pricing-engine-local fault. order-service is the client; market-data-service is flat (0.2% error, ~40ms p99); redis-cache is flat on every available proxy (hit ratio 93.8-98.5%, cpu 20-24%, clients ~312, evictions ~3/min, F37-F41/F47); portfolio-service and api-gateway error_rate flat at ~0.2% through onset (F42).

Alternatives: H3 (traffic-driven) is refuted by flat request_rate with a 2.5x CPU step (F20/F21/F22/F25/F28). H4 (shared redis-cache/infra) is refuted by redis-cache health across all available proxies plus the absence of any cache/IO/connection error signature (F37-F42, F44, F47). H5 (external dependency) is refuted by the CPU-bound compute fingerprint with no transport errors, and market-data-service flat. H2 (the reporter's serialization suspicion) is refuted by timing (9-minute offset, baseline through the deploy minute) and signature (compute deadline, no parse errors). The one residual gap in H4's refutation (auth-service/payment-service never measured) is a blast-radius completeness gap, not a live competitor: it cannot explain the pricing-engine-local CPU/Monte-Carlo signature or produce the observed recovery-free saturation tied to a pricing-engine flag, and the two measured fan-out services are flat.

Data quality: the only notable partials (first config-changes query partial with shard 2/3 down, missing restart_count/latency redis metrics) are either retried with consistent results (F31/F32 second query; 'restarts'=0 flat, F24) or are permanently unavailable metric names (tool reliability notes), so no conclusion rests on silently-truncated data.

Calibration: the residual risk is entirely the inferential mechanism hop plus the unmeasured config-shard and auth/payment fan-out. A defensible confidence is 0.85; the stated 0.82 sits slightly below that and is well-calibrated. No blocking issue remains and, as the final round, no further query is available or would change the ranking.

H1 is adequately proven for the purpose of an active SEV-2 root cause. The causal chain now rests on verified findings at every hop except one explicitly-labelled mechanism link, and every competing hypothesis has been tested and contradicted by data rather than dismissed by argument.

Grounding: cfg-3120 (pricing-engine flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5->100, 12:04:00Z, pm-experiments) is verified with exact timestamp, and F31/F32 show it is the only change after 11:56Z and was never rolled back or reduced. The outcome side is verified at 60s resolution: CPU 38.22% (12:04) -> 98.65% (12:05) and p99 60.53ms -> 2534.9ms (12:05), same minute (F26/F27), with pricing-engine error_rate following one minute later 0.15% -> 12.98% (F29) and holding ~12.5% (F23); order-service's only error type is the 2500ms pricing-engine quote timeout, first at 12:06:10Z (F13/F43/F44), with p99 pinned just above the 2500ms budget (F45) and a single error step at the same 12:05Z bucket (F46). The fingerprint on the failing path is an internal compute deadline, 'GreeksV2Calculator: Monte-Carlo paths=20000 took 6465ms' and 'deadline exceeded computing quote calculator=GreeksV2', with zero connection-refused/parse/deserialization errors anywhere (F17/F43/F44). The one non-verified link (flag ramp -> the measured CPU is the Greeks v2 path) is honestly declared as an assumption; it is corroborated by exact-minute timing, flat offered load (F20/F21/F28), the compute-bound log signature, and the analogue precedent HIST-101 (F36). No per-flag metric exists in this dataset, so this cannot be closed by any query; that is a residual inferential hop, not a missing check.

Temporal order: onset is localized to the single minute bucket 12:05:00Z, one minute after the 12:04:00Z flag ramp and nine minutes after the 11:56:00Z market-data deploy; every minute 11:50-12:04Z is at baseline including the deploy minute (F26/F27/F30). The proposed cause immediately precedes onset.

Scope: the blast radius is fully explained by a pricing-engine-local fault. order-service is the client; market-data-service is flat (0.2% error, ~40ms p99); redis-cache is flat on every available proxy (hit ratio 93.8-98.5%, cpu 20-24%, clients ~312, evictions ~3/min, F37-F41/F47); portfolio-service and api-gateway error_rate flat at ~0.2% through onset (F42).

Alternatives: H3 (traffic-driven) is refuted by flat request_rate with a 2.5x CPU step (F20/F21/F22/F25/F28). H4 (shared redis-cache/infra) is refuted by redis-cache health across all available proxies plus the absence of any cache/IO/connection error signature (F37-F42, F44, F47). H5 (external dependency) is refuted by the CPU-bound compute fingerprint with no transport errors, and market-data-service flat. H2 (the reporter's serialization suspicion) is refuted by timing (9-minute offset, baseline through the deploy minute) and signature (compute deadline, no parse errors). The one residual gap in H4's refutation (auth-service/payment-service never measured) is a blast-radius completeness gap, not a live competitor: it cannot explain the pricing-engine-local CPU/Monte-Carlo signature or produce the observed recovery-free saturation tied to a pricing-engine flag, and the two measured fan-out services are flat.

Data quality: the only notable partials (first config-changes query partial with shard 2/3 down, missing restart_count/latency redis metrics) are either retried with consistent results (F31/F32 second query; 'restarts'=0 flat, F24) or are permanently unavailable metric names (tool reliability notes), so no conclusion rests on silently-truncated data.

Calibration: the residual risk is entirely the inferential mechanism hop plus the unmeasured config-shard and auth/payment fan-out. A defensible confidence is 0.85; the stated 0.82 sits slightly below that and is well-calibrated. No blocking issue remains and, as the final round, no further query is available or would change the ranking.

This is a real gap but not blocking: it cannot be closed by any query in this dataset and is corroborated by exact-minute timing, flat load, the compute-bound log signature, and HIST-101.
